incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (MSS and PLA-linked)
incidents.vector: A China-based front company (Nanjing Xinjiuwei) ran the 'QScan' vulnerability scanner and 'QTRouter' obfuscation botnet to breach networks by exploiting flaws in Ivanti, Fortinet, Citrix, Pulse Secure, F5 and other products.
incidents.impact: The DOJ said the QTFY group had compromised the Federal Reserve, DOE, DOJ, NASA, NIH and HHS since 2018 and attempted to breach the U.S. Senate; the FBI seized three domains, rendering both hacking platforms inoperable.

incidents.vector: The medical device manufacturer disclosed a cyberattack; the initial access method and threat actor have not been identified.
incidents.impact: The incident disrupted the company's shipment and order-processing operations.

incidents.victim: Exposed enterprise AI infrastructure (LiteLLM, RAGFlow, Kestra)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited internet-exposed AI gateway and orchestration services (LiteLLM via CVE-2026-42271/CVE-2026-48710, plus RAGFlow and Kestra) to run code, harvest secrets from process environments and reach backend databases.
incidents.impact: Microsoft observed credential theft (model-provider keys, database strings), PostgreSQL data collection, XMRig cryptominer deployment and SSH-key persistence across compromised AI workloads.

incidents.vector: The 'NovaCookies' adversary-in-the-middle phishing service relays Microsoft 365 logins in real time using Docusign lures and legitimate Microsoft/Google redirects, stealing authenticated session cookies to bypass MFA.
incidents.impact: The rented kit uses at least 755 domains and targets hundreds of organizations, more than half in the U.S.; stolen sessions let attackers into accounts without triggering typical login anomalies.

incidents.vector: The Akira ransomware group breached the benefits-administration platform's network and exfiltrated files over a five-day window in November 2025.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole Social Security numbers, financial account details, health insurance and medical data, passport numbers and taxpayer IDs; more than 64,000 people in South Carolina alone were affected, and class actions are forming.

incidents.vector: A large distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack flooded the infrastructure of Digdir's IT partner, Vivicta.
incidents.impact: The attack knocked out roughly 10 digital services including the ID-porten identity gateway (4.5M+ users), disrupting logins to public services and parts of Norway's health and e-prescription systems for over 30 hours; it was the third DDoS on Digdir since June.

incidents.victim: West African cybercrime networks (Black Axe and affiliates)
incidents.vector: Interpol's eight-month Operation Jackal IV mapped and disrupted crime-as-a-service infrastructure — domains, money-laundering networks and call-center investment/romance scam operations across 22 countries.
incidents.impact: Police made 58 arrests and identified 263 more suspects; seizures included $2.67M in South Africa and $379K plus properties in Romania, while an Argentine crime-as-a-service network of 196 people was uncovered.

incidents.vector: An actor using the persona 'CyberLeek' obtained pre-release Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay footage — likely via direct access to Rockstar systems or an insider — and drip-published it a week before the planned reveal.
incidents.impact: The leaks became one of the year's highest-profile extortion cases; the actor monetized via a memecoin and watermarked crypto wallet links, prompting Take-Two to obtain DMCA subpoenas against Discord, Microsoft and X.

incidents.vector: The UK disclosed an Iranian cyberattack against a power plant; the incident prompted a proposed amendment to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill to ban critical-sector purchases from foreign adversaries.
incidents.impact: The attack forced the power plant offline for four days the previous month.

incidents.vector: The Iran-based Mabna Institute ran spearphishing campaigns against professor accounts on behalf of the IRGC; DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment against 17 members and Treasury imposed new sanctions.
incidents.impact: The campaign compromised ~8,000 professor accounts across 144 U.S. and 178 foreign universities, stealing at least 31.5 terabytes of academic data and intellectual property; a $10M reward was offered for five defendants.

incidents.vector: The pro-Kremlin hacktivist group NoName057 compiled and published personnel data on Telegram, citing Spain's support for Ukraine.
incidents.impact: The group leaked the names of nearly 1,000 members of the Spanish military and police forces.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the road traffic agency's systems; the intrusion method was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole personal information, payment receipts and license plate details on 1.2 million Latvian citizens going back to 2008; the agency's leadership resigned following the hack.

incidents.victim: Rust open-source ecosystem (arrayref and two other crates)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a prominent Rust developer and injected malware into three of his libraries in a supply-chain attack; Wiz linked the infrastructure to North Korean operations.
incidents.impact: The malicious versions were live for only 23 minutes, but one affected crate (arrayref) has nearly 5 million weekly downloads; the Rust security team removed the versions and locked the account.

incidents.vector: Slovakia's NBU found that NERO R-ONE traffic cameras — a rebranded Russian CORDON PRO.M model — contained a backdoor granting shell and network access via SMS from hardcoded Russian phone numbers, plus disabled SecureBoot and exposed live streams.
incidents.impact: The €30M EU-funded project intended to deploy 279 cameras; officials paused installation and ordered an independent audit after the backdoor was disclosed. Similar devices are reportedly installed in Croatia and other Eastern European states.

incidents.vector: The electronic health record company disclosed a data breach; details of the intrusion were not provided.
incidents.impact: The company said 3.7 million people were affected by the breach.

incidents.vector: A cyberattack hit the Berlin city government; IT staff disconnected affected agencies from the city network to contain it.
incidents.impact: The attack took down emails, remote gateways and internet connectivity across the transport and urban development departments.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack struck Winnipeg's largest hospital, affecting building and facility control systems.
incidents.impact: The attack disabled access doors and HVAC systems, forcing the hospital to increase onsite security; the hospital said patient care and clinical operations were not impacted.

incidents.victim: University of Texas at San Antonio
incidents.vector: The university took IT systems offline following a security breach over the weekend; the intrusion vector was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: UTSA extended tuition payment deadlines and planned to reset all user account passwords once systems were restored; classes were expected to start on schedule.

incidents.victim: Global employers hiring remote IT staff (1,100+ companies)
incidents.vector: Recorded Future's 'PurpleDelta' cluster of North Korean IT workers, likely based in China, used 22+ fabricated personas, AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants and forged IDs to secure remote technical jobs, applying to 60+ positions a day.
incidents.impact: Operators applied to over 1,100 companies and were likely employed at 10 or more, funneling wages to the North Korean regime and posing an active insider-threat and supply-chain risk to hiring organizations.

incidents.vector: An Iranian hacktivist group calling itself the '313 Team' launched DDoS attacks against the two platforms on consecutive days.
incidents.impact: The attacks caused prolonged outages at both Bluesky and GitHub; the group had run a prior DDoS wave in April.

incidents.vector: Hackers stole customer data from an external analytics service provider used by Israel's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
incidents.impact: The data of 250,000 customers was compromised; the company did not specify what type of data was taken.

incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese hackers used publicly available AI tools, chaining Hermes and OpenClaw agents to automate reconnaissance, intrusion, lateral movement and data exfiltration against government networks across Asia.
incidents.impact: The campaign breached Taiwanese government networks and Thailand's Ministry of Finance as part of a broader wave targeting multiple Asian governments.
